questions.question_en: _____ does NOT have any child ClassLoaders.
questions.explanation_en: Java's class loaders form a parent-child chain: Bootstrap (also called Primordial) is the parent of the Extension loader, and Extension is the parent of the System (Application) class loader. The System ClassLoader sits at the bottom of the built-in chain, so it has no child loaders of its own. Bootstrap/Primordial is the root, so it does have a child (Extension).

questions.explanation_en: Integer and String are class names, not reserved keywords, so they can legally be used as variable names. The code prints the int 24 and then the char 'I' with print (no newline), so the output is 24I. There is no compiler error.

questions.question_en: Which of the following is the execution engine for .NET applications and serves as the interface between .NET applications and the operating system.
questions.explanation_en: The Common Language Runtime (CLR) is the .NET execution engine. It loads managed code, compiles it with the JIT compiler, and handles memory (garbage collection), security and exceptions, acting between the application and the OS. FCL is the class library, and CTS/CLS are type and language rules, not runtimes.

questions.question_en: The technology of .Net is developed by ______ and was launched in ______.
questions.explanation_en: The .NET Framework was developed by Microsoft. Version 1.0 was released in 2002 (beta versions came out in 2000-2001). Oracle and Google did not build .NET, and 2010 is when .NET 4.0 came out, not the launch.

questions.chapter: Programming — Programming Basics: Data Types, Operators & Control Flow
questions.explanation_en: In Java an integer literal that starts with 0 is octal, so 017 = 1*8 + 7 = 15 in decimal. The loop prints each element followed by a space: 121 201 15. (The curly quotes in the question are just printing errors for normal " " quotes.) Option 1 forgets the octal rule.

questions.chapter: Programming — Programming Basics: Data Types, Operators & Control Flow
questions.question_en: Which of the following operators has the highest precedence in the C programming language?
questions.explanation_en: In C, parentheses () (function call/grouping) have the highest precedence. Next come unary operators, then *, /, %, and after them the relational, equality (!=) and bitwise XOR (^) operators. So () is evaluated first.

questions.question_en: C++ provides inline functions to facilitate a reduced function call overhead mainly for ______.
questions.explanation_en: An inline function's body is copied into the place where it is called, which saves the cost of a call (pushing arguments, jumping, returning). This is worth it only for small functions. For large functions it bloats the code, and the compiler may ignore the inline request.

questions.chapter: Programming — Programming Basics: Data Types, Operators & Control Flow
questions.question_en: Which of the following is a java primitive data type?
questions.explanation_en: Java has 8 primitive types: byte, short, int, long, float, double, char and boolean. Arrays, String and classes are reference (non-primitive) types. So byte is the primitive type here.

questions.question_en: Which of the following controls in VB.NET is used to select one option from a number of choices?
questions.explanation_en: RadioButtons in a group are mutually exclusive, so the user can pick exactly one option from several choices. A ListBox can also allow multiple selection, a Label only displays text, and a Button triggers an action.

questions.question_en: Which of the following is FALSE with reference to constructor in C#.NET?

options.en: It can have a return type.
All classes have constructors by default.
Constructor name must match the class name.
The constructor is called when the object is created.

questions.explanation_en: In C# a constructor cannot have any return type, not even void, so statement 1 is false. The other statements are true: a default constructor is provided if you write none, it has the same name as the class, and it runs when an object is created.

questions.question_en: Which of the following statements is FALSE?

options.en: "static public void main(String…abcd){}" is a valid statement.

questions.explanation_en: A final method cannot be overridden in a subclass; that is the whole purpose of the final keyword. So statement 1 is false. The others are true: modifier order and varargs make 'static public void main(String... abcd)' valid, abstract classes cannot be instantiated, and Java 8+ interfaces allow default methods.

As printed, the string literal "Hello World is broken across a line. A C string literal cannot contain a raw newline, so the compiler reports a missing terminating quote, which is a compilation error. If it had been written with the escape \n, then 6 + "Hello World\n" would point 6 characters into the string and print 'World' (option 3).

questions.question_en: In C, variable list arguments are denoted by the standard header:
questions.explanation_en: Variable argument lists in C (va_list, va_start, va_arg, va_end) are declared in the standard header <stdarg.h>. <stdio.h> only declares functions that use them, such as printf and vprintf. The official key (<stdio.h>) looks wrong; option 4, <stdarg.h>, is correct.

questions.chapter: Programming — Programming Basics: Data Types, Operators & Control Flow
questions.question_en: scanf() is a predefined function in which of the following header files?
questions.explanation_en: scanf() and printf() are standard input/output functions declared in <stdio.h>. <string.h> has string functions such as strlen, <ctype.h> has character tests such as isdigit, and <unistd.h> is a POSIX header.

questions.question_en: Which access modifier can be used to access members in deriving class?
questions.explanation_en: Protected members can be accessed inside the class and in classes derived from it (subclasses), but not by unrelated outside code. Private members are not accessible in derived classes. Public members are accessible there too, but they are open to everyone, so protected is the modifier designed for derived-class access. Void is a return type, not an access modifier.

questions.question_en: What is the name of the .NET collection class that enables an element to be accessed using a unique key?
questions.explanation_en: System.Collections.Hashtable stores key/value pairs and lets you get an element by its unique key, using hashing. ArrayList and linked lists are accessed by position (index or traversal), not by key.

questions.chapter: Programming — Python: Data Types, Collections, File Handling & Pandas
questions.question_en: Which of the following type of function used with strings in the Python language returns the character with the highest ASCII value?
questions.explanation_en: When given a string, Python's max() returns the character with the highest ASCII/Unicode value, for example max('apple') = 'p'. len() returns the length, and hvalue() and long() are not Python built-ins for strings.

questions.chapter: Programming — Python: Data Types, Collections, File Handling & Pandas
questions.question_en:
Select the correct output for the following python code?
a = 20
b = 35
if a >= b:
    print("yes")
else:
    print("No")
questions.explanation_en: a = 20 and b = 35, so a >= b is False and the else branch runs, printing No. The output keeps the capital N exactly as written in the string. The code is valid, so there is no syntax error.

questions.chapter: Programming — Python: Data Types, Collections, File Handling & Pandas
questions.question_en: In Python language, which of the following method of lists is used to add an element to the end of the list?
questions.explanation_en: list.append(x) adds x at the end of the list. pop() removes (and returns) an element, sort() arranges the elements in order, and index() returns the position of a value.

questions.chapter: Programming — Python: Data Types, Collections, File Handling & Pandas
questions.question_en: In Python language, which of following mode for opening the file, opens the file for both reading and writing and file pointer will be placed at the start of the file?
questions.explanation_en: Mode 'r+' opens an existing file for both reading and writing with the file pointer at the beginning. 'a+' also allows reading and writing, but writes go to the end of the file. 'rb' is read-only binary and 'ab' is append-only binary.

questions.chapter: Programming — Python: Data Types, Collections, File Handling & Pandas
questions.question_en: The values in a dictionary can be ______ but the keys in the dictionary should be ______ in Python programming languages
questions.explanation_en: In a Python dictionary the values can repeat (for example {'a': 1, 'b': 1}), but the keys must be unique (and immutable). If a key is assigned again, the old value is replaced, so a key never appears twice.

questions.chapter: Programming — Python: Data Types, Collections, File Handling & Pandas
questions.question_en: Which of the following is a one-dimensional labelled array capable of holding any data type (integers, strings, floating point numbers, python objects, etc) in data handling with pandas?
questions.explanation_en: A pandas Series is a one-dimensional labelled array that can hold any data type, with an index as its labels. A DataFrame is two-dimensional (rows and columns, made of several Series).

questions.chapter: Programming — Python: Data Types, Collections, File Handling & Pandas
questions.question_en: Data frame in Pandas has a method which takes a column name (for a regular index) or a list of column names to create a new, re-indexed data frame, which of the following is correct method?
questions.explanation_en: DataFrame.set_index() takes a column name (or a list of column names for a MultiIndex) and returns a new DataFrame indexed by those columns. reset_index() does the reverse. data.index is an attribute, not a method that re-indexes, and 'dFb'/'dFmi' are just variable names.

questions.chapter: Programming — Python: Data Types, Collections, File Handling & Pandas
questions.question_en: Which of the following symbol is used to add comments in the Python language?
questions.explanation_en: In Python a single-line comment starts with the hash symbol #, and everything after it on the line is ignored. // is used for comments in C/C++/Java, but in Python it is the floor-division operator.

questions.chapter: Programming — Python: Data Types, Collections, File Handling & Pandas
questions.question_en: Extensions like .txt, .py, .CSV, etc in python language are example of ______.
questions.explanation_en: .txt, .py and .csv files store data as human-readable characters, so they are text files, unlike binary files such as .jpg or .exe. ASCII and Unicode are character encodings, not file types, and a text editor is a program used to edit these files.

questions.chapter: Programming — Programming Basics: Data Types, Operators & Control Flow
questions.question_en: Number with decimal points is called ______ in programming language.
questions.explanation_en: Numbers with a decimal point (like 3.14) are fractional numbers, stored as floating-point (real) numbers in programming languages such as float in Python. Among the given options 'fractional point numbers' is the matching term. Integers have no fractional part, and complex/imaginary numbers have a different meaning.

questions.chapter: Programming — Python: Data Types, Collections, File Handling & Pandas
questions.question_en: Which symbol is used to add the comment in the code or program to make it more readable and understandable in Python programming language?
questions.explanation_en: Python uses # for comments: everything after # on a line is ignored by the interpreter and is only for readers of the code. * is multiplication, - is subtraction and : starts a code block.

questions.chapter: Programming — Python: Data Types, Collections, File Handling & Pandas
questions.question_en: ______ files are spreadsheet files in a text format of data when cell contents are separated by a character for example a comma or semi-colon.
questions.explanation_en: CSV (Comma-Separated Values) files are plain-text spreadsheet files in which each line is a row and the cell values are separated by a delimiter, usually a comma (sometimes a semicolon). 'CVS' is a misspelling, and 'Semi-colon Separated Values' is not the standard name of the format.

questions.question_en: _____ is a code that consists of CPU and platform-independent set of instructions, which can be easily converted to the native code.
questions.explanation_en: In .NET, source code is compiled into MSIL (Microsoft Intermediate Language), a CPU- and platform-independent instruction set. At run time the JIT compiler converts MSIL into native machine code. JIT is the converter, not the code itself, so MSIL is the answer.

questions.question_en: In C++ language, the instruction 'ignore(x,y);' _______ .

options.en: skips the last x characters and stops if character y is encountered
skips the first y characters and stops if character x is encountered
skips the first x characters and stops if character y is encountered
skips the last y characters and stops if character x is encountered

questions.explanation_en: istream::ignore(n, delim) extracts and discards up to n characters from the input stream, stopping earlier if the delimiter character is encountered (the delimiter is also discarded). So ignore(x, y) skips the first x characters and stops at character y. It works on the next (first) characters in the stream, not the last ones.

questions.question_en: Select the true statement about try-catch blocks.

options.en: A try block must have at least 1 catch to have a finally block.
A try block must have only 1 finally block for each catch block.
A try block can have many catches but only 1 finally block.
A try block can have many catches and many finally blocks.

questions.explanation_en: A try block may be followed by multiple catch blocks (one per exception type) but at most one finally block. Option 1 is false because try-finally without any catch is legal, and options 2 and 4 wrongly allow multiple finally blocks.

questions.question_en: Which of the following is FALSE about packages?

options.en: Packages are used to prevent naming conflicts.
Packages are used to prevent naming conflicts, and packages are considered data encapsulation.

questions.explanation_en: Packages DO provide controlled access through access modifiers (default/package-private and protected), so statement 1 is FALSE. Packages also prevent naming conflicts and support encapsulation by grouping related classes.

questions.question_en: Which of the following is a relational operator in the C programming language?
questions.explanation_en: != (not equal to) is a relational operator in C, along with <, >, <=, >= and ==. &&, || and ! are logical operators.
y = &x, so *y = 8. The expression x * *y * x + *y = 8 * 8 * 8 + 8 = 512 + 8 = 520. There is no compilation or runtime error because y is a valid pointer to x.

questions.chapter: Programming — Programming Basics: Data Types, Operators & Control Flow
questions.question_en: Which of the following is a symbolic name given to a memory location in any programming language?
questions.explanation_en: A variable is a symbolic name given to a memory location whose value can change during program execution. A constant/literal is a fixed value, and an attribute is a property of an object or entity.

questions.chapter: Programming — Programming Basics: Data Types, Operators & Control Flow
questions.question_en: Which of the following is NOT a storage class in the C programming language?
questions.explanation_en: C has four storage classes: auto, register, static and extern. 'intern' is not a storage class or keyword in C.

questions.question_en: Identify the descending order of strict access protection.
questions.explanation_en: Key doubt: from strictest to least strict, Java access levels are private (class only) > package/default (same package) > protected (same package + subclasses) > public (everywhere), which is option 4. Protected is less strict than package access because it adds subclass access outside the package. The official option 2 wrongly ranks protected as stricter than package.

questions.question_en: What feature of OOP allows an instance of a class to take on many forms?
questions.explanation_en: Polymorphism ('many forms') lets the same name/operator behave differently; operator overloading is a compile-time form of polymorphism where one operator works on many types. 'Operator overriding' is not a standard term, and multiple inheritance or nested classes are not about many forms.

questions.chapter: Programming — Python: Data Types, Collections, File Handling & Pandas
questions.question_en: Which of the following type conversion function in the Python language, is used to convert a character into an integer?
questions.explanation_en: ord() returns the integer Unicode code of a character, e.g. ord('A') = 65 (chr() does the reverse). tuple(), dict() and set() convert iterables into those collection types.

questions.chapter: Programming — Python: Data Types, Collections, File Handling & Pandas
questions.question_en: In Python language, which of the following is correct for 'strip ( )' function?

options.en: It returns the string by removing trailing and leading white spaces
It returns a list from the string depending upon the delimiter that we specify
It returns the power of values passed
It returns the string with the first character in upper case and lowering the case for rest of the string

questions.explanation_en: str.strip() returns a copy of the string with leading and trailing whitespace removed. split() returns a list based on a delimiter (option 2), pow() gives power (option 3), and capitalize() uppercases the first character (option 4).

questions.chapter: Programming — Python: Data Types, Collections, File Handling & Pandas
questions.question_en:
Choose the correct output for the following Python code.
tuple_var_mix = ("Example", 1, "Tuple")
print (tuple_var_mix)
questions.explanation_en: print() on a tuple shows it in parentheses with strings in quotes: ('Example', 1, 'Tuple'). Curly braces indicate a set/dict and square brackets a list, and Python preserves the case of 'Tuple'.

questions.chapter: Programming — Python: Data Types, Collections, File Handling & Pandas
questions.question_en: ______ is a two-dimensional labelled data structure with columns of potentially different type, in data handling with pandas.
questions.explanation_en: A DataFrame is a two-dimensional labelled data structure with rows and columns, where columns may hold different data types (like a spreadsheet or SQL table). A Series is one-dimensional.

questions.question_en:
If you encounter an import Error, what does it mean?
I. Python could find pandas in list of available libraries
II. Python couldn't find python in list of available libraries
III. Python couldn't find Pandas in list of available libraries
questions.explanation_en: An ImportError/ModuleNotFoundError while doing import pandas means Python could not find the pandas package among installed libraries (e.g. it is not installed). Statement I says it could find pandas, and II refers to 'python' instead of the library, so only III is correct.

questions.chapter: Programming — Python: Data Types, Collections, File Handling & Pandas
questions.question_en: Which of the following is correct for Identifiers name used in Python language?

options.en: An identifier can have underscore (_) symbol
We must use keywords as identifier
There is restriction the length of an identifier
An identifier must start with a digit

questions.explanation_en: A Python identifier can contain letters, digits and the underscore (_), and may start with an underscore. Keywords cannot be used as identifiers, there is no length limit, and an identifier cannot start with a digit.

questions.chapter: Programming — Python: Data Types, Collections, File Handling & Pandas
questions.question_en: Which operation is provided in Pandas, when multiple tables can be concatenated both column wise and row wise as database?
questions.explanation_en: Pandas provides database-style operations to combine tables: merge() (join on keys) and concat() for row-wise or column-wise joining. Among the options, MERGE is the combining operation; SUM, GROUP BY and SELECT aggregate or filter data rather than combining tables.

questions.question_en:
String is a collection of one or more character which consists of ______ in programming language.
I. Letters
II. Numbers
III. Symbols
questions.explanation_en: A string is a sequence of characters, which can include letters, digits (numbers as characters) and symbols such as @, # or spaces. So all three - I, II and III - are correct.

questions.chapter: Programming — Programming Basics: Data Types, Operators & Control Flow
questions.question_en: How many primitive data types are defined in Java?
questions.explanation_en: Java has exactly eight primitive types: byte, short, int, long, float, double, char and boolean. String, arrays and classes are reference types, not primitives.

questions.chapter: Programming — Programming Basics: Data Types, Operators & Control Flow
questions.explanation_en: A byte holds -128 to 127, and a narrowing cast keeps only the low 8 bits. 200 does not fit, so it wraps to 200 - 256 = -56. Likewise 130 becomes 130 - 256 = -126.

questions.chapter: Programming — Programming Basics: Data Types, Operators & Control Flow
questions.explanation_en: In C (C99 onwards) integer division truncates toward zero, so -23 / 4 = -5.75 becomes -5. The remainder follows a == (a/b)*b + a%b, so -23 % 4 = -23 - (-20) = -3. The remainder takes the sign of the dividend; -6 1 would be Python's floor-division result.

questions.chapter: Programming — Programming Basics: Data Types, Operators & Control Flow
questions.question_en:
What is the output of the following Python 3 code?
```python
print(7 / 2, -17 // 5, -17 % 5)
```
questions.explanation_en: In Python 3, / is true division, so 7 / 2 = 3.5. // is floor division: -17 / 5 = -3.4, floored down to -4. % takes the sign of the divisor, so -17 % 5 = -17 - (-4*5) = 3.

questions.chapter: Programming — Programming Basics: Data Types, Operators & Control Flow
questions.question_en: In Java, given `byte b = 10;`, which of the following statements causes a compilation error?
questions.explanation_en: In b + 5 the byte is promoted to int, so the result is an int, and an int cannot be assigned to a byte without an explicit cast. Compound assignment (+=) and ++ include an automatic cast back to byte, so they compile. The explicit (byte) cast also compiles.

questions.chapter: Programming — Programming Basics: Data Types, Operators & Control Flow
questions.explanation_en: + is evaluated left to right. 1 + 2 are both ints, so they add to 3. 3 + "3" is a String, "33", and from then on every + is concatenation: "334", then "3345".

questions.chapter: Programming — Programming Basics: Data Types, Operators & Control Flow
questions.explanation_en: j = i++ stores the old value 10 in j, then i becomes 11. k = ++i first makes i 12, then stores 12 in k. So i = 12, j = 10, k = 12.

questions.chapter: Programming — Programming Basics: Data Types, Operators & Control Flow
questions.explanation_en: In Java, i = i++ first saves the old value of i (0), then increments i to 1, and finally assigns the saved 0 back to i. So each pass leaves i at 0. After four passes it is still 0.

questions.chapter: Programming — Programming Basics: Data Types, Operators & Control Flow
questions.explanation_en: *, / and % have higher precedence than + and -, and they group left to right. b * c / 2 = 12 / 2 = 6 and a % b = 10 % 4 = 2. Then 10 - 6 + 2 = 6.

questions.chapter: Programming — Programming Basics: Data Types, Operators & Control Flow
questions.explanation_en: Relational operators give 1 (true) or 0 (false) and group left to right. 10 > x > 2 is (10 > 5) > 2, which is 1 > 2, so 0. In the second expression > has higher precedence than ==, so it is (10 > 5) == 1, which is 1 == 1, so 1.

questions.chapter: Programming — Programming Basics: Data Types, Operators & Control Flow
questions.explanation_en: || and && evaluate left to right with a sequence point after the left operand. b++ gives 0 (false) and b becomes 1, so a-- is evaluated: it gives 2 (true) and a becomes 1. The left side of && is therefore 1, so ++b runs: b becomes 2, which is true. A logical result is always 0 or 1, so c = 1, giving 1 2 1.

questions.chapter: Programming — Programming Basics: Data Types, Operators & Control Flow
questions.explanation_en: && short-circuits: a > 5 is false, so ++a is skipped and a stays 3; r is false. & on booleans always evaluates both sides, so ++a runs and a becomes 4, but false & true is still false. Output: 4 false false.

questions.chapter: Programming — Programming Basics: Data Types, Operators & Control Flow
questions.explanation_en: In binary a = 1100 and b = 1010. AND gives 1000 = 8, OR gives 1110 = 14, and XOR (1 where the bits differ) gives 0110 = 6.

questions.chapter: Programming — Programming Basics: Data Types, Operators & Control Flow
questions.explanation_en: In two's complement ~x equals -(x + 1), so ~5 = -6. x << 3 multiplies by 2^3: 5 * 8 = 40. x >> 1 divides a positive value by 2 and drops the fraction: 5 >> 1 = 2.

questions.chapter: Programming — Programming Basics: Data Types, Operators & Control Flow
questions.explanation_en: >> is the signed right shift: it copies the sign bit, so -16 >> 2 = -16 / 4 = -4. >>> is the unsigned right shift: it fills with zeros. -16 is 0xFFFFFFF0, and shifting it right by 28 leaves the top four 1-bits, 1111 = 15.

questions.chapter: Programming — Programming Basics: Data Types, Operators & Control Flow
questions.question_en:
What is the output of the following Python 3 code?
```python
print(2 ** 3 ** 2, -2 ** 2)
```
questions.explanation_en: ** is right-associative, so 2 ** 3 ** 2 = 2 ** (3 ** 2) = 2 ** 9 = 512. ** also binds more tightly than unary minus, so -2 ** 2 = -(2 ** 2) = -4.

questions.chapter: Programming — Programming Basics: Data Types, Operators & Control Flow

questions.chapter: Programming — Programming Basics: Data Types, Operators & Control Flow
questions.question_en: In C, which format specifier must be used with scanf() to read a value into a variable of type double?
questions.explanation_en: scanf() needs a pointer of the exact type. %f expects a float *, %lf expects a double * and %Lf expects a long double *. (In printf(), %f works for double too, because float arguments are promoted to double.)

questions.chapter: Programming — Programming Basics: Data Types, Operators & Control Flow
questions.question_en: In C, the library functions sqrt() and pow() are declared in which header file?
questions.explanation_en: Mathematical functions such as sqrt(), pow(), sin() and floor() are declared in <math.h>. stdio.h holds input/output functions like printf() and scanf(), and stdlib.h holds functions like malloc() and atoi().

questions.chapter: Programming — Programming Basics: Data Types, Operators & Control Flow
questions.question_en: In C, which operation is NOT allowed on a variable declared with the register storage class?

options.en: Taking its address with the & operator
Assigning a new value to it
Using it as a loop counter
Passing its value to a function

questions.explanation_en: register asks the compiler to keep the variable in a CPU register for fast access. Because a register has no memory address, the C standard forbids applying & to a register variable, even if the compiler actually keeps it in memory. Reading, assigning and passing its value are all allowed.

questions.chapter: Programming — Programming Basics: Data Types, Operators & Control Flow
questions.question_en: Which of the following is NOT a keyword in C?
questions.explanation_en: volatile, sizeof and register are all reserved C keywords (sizeof is a keyword that works as an operator). include is not a keyword; #include is a preprocessor directive handled before compilation.

questions.chapter: Programming — Programming Basics: Data Types, Operators & Control Flow
questions.question_en: Which of the following is NOT a reserved keyword in Java?

questions.question_en: Compared with an equivalent iterative (loop) solution, a recursive function usually

options.en: runs faster, because no loop is needed
uses more memory, as every call adds a stack frame
cannot return a value to its caller

questions.explanation_en: In tail recursion nothing is left to do after the recursive call returns, so compilers can reuse the same stack frame (tail-call optimisation). Head recursion makes the call first and works afterwards, indirect recursion is A calling B calling A, and nested recursion passes a recursive call as an argument.

add(1)

questions.question_en: A 2-D array int A[10][20] is stored in row-major order starting at address 2000, and each int takes 4 bytes. What is the address of A[3][5] (indices start at 0)?
questions.explanation_en: In row-major order, Address = Base + (i * columns + j) * size. Here that is 2000 + (3 * 20 + 5) * 4 = 2000 + 65 * 4 = 2260. 2212 is the column-major answer, (5 * 10 + 3) * 4 + 2000.

questions.question_en: An array B[1..10][1..15] (10 rows, 15 columns) is stored in column-major order. The base address is 500 and each element takes 2 bytes. What is the address of B[4][6]?
questions.explanation_en: In column-major order with lower bounds 1, Address = Base + ((j - 1) * rows + (i - 1)) * size. That is 500 + ((6 - 1) * 10 + (4 - 1)) * 2 = 500 + 53 * 2 = 606. 600 is the row-major result, 500 + (3 * 15 + 5) * 2.
The array size is taken from the 6 initialisers. sizeof(a) is the whole array, 6 * 4 = 24 bytes, and sizeof(a[0]) is one int, 4 bytes. 24 / 4 = 6, the number of elements.

questions.question_en: In C, an int pointer p holds the address 1000. If sizeof(int) is 4, what address does p + 3 hold?
questions.explanation_en: Adding n to a pointer moves it by n elements, not n bytes. For an int pointer each step is sizeof(int) = 4 bytes, so p + 3 = 1000 + 3 * 4 = 1012.

questions.question_en: In C, an array int a[10] is passed to a function declared as void f(int arr[]). What does sizeof(arr) give inside f()?

options.en: 40, the size of the whole array
The size of an int pointer, not of the array

questions.explanation_en: An array argument decays to a pointer to its first element, and a parameter written as int arr[] is really int *arr. So sizeof(arr) inside f() is the size of a pointer (4 or 8 bytes), not 10 * sizeof(int). That is why the length is usually passed as a separate argument.

questions.question_en: Which C header file declares the functions strlen(), strcpy() and strcmp()?
questions.explanation_en: The string-handling functions such as strlen(), strcpy(), strcat(), strcmp() and strchr() are declared in <string.h>. ctype.h holds character tests like isdigit() and toupper(), and stdlib.h holds malloc(), atoi() and similar.

questions.question_en: What is the main difference between malloc() and calloc() in C?

options.en: malloc() sets the allocated bytes to zero; calloc() does not
calloc() allocates on the stack; malloc() on the heap
Only memory from malloc() has to be released with free()
calloc() sets the allocated bytes to zero; malloc() does not

questions.explanation_en: Both allocate memory on the heap and both blocks must be released with free(). calloc(n, size) allocates n * size bytes and fills them with zero. malloc(size) leaves the contents uninitialised (garbage).

questions.question_en: What does malloc() return in C when the requested memory cannot be allocated?
questions.explanation_en: malloc(), calloc() and realloc() return NULL when they cannot allocate the requested block. A program should therefore check the returned pointer against NULL before using it.

questions.question_en: Given int a[5]; int *p = a; in C, which of the following statements is INVALID?
questions.explanation_en: An array name stands for the fixed address of its first element and is not a modifiable lvalue, so a++ (or a = p) is a compilation error. p is an ordinary pointer variable, so p++ is fine. *(a + 1) = 3 and a[0] = a[1] only change elements, which is allowed.

questions.question_en: In C, what does the declaration int *const p = &x; mean?

options.en: *p cannot be changed, but p can point elsewhere
p cannot be changed, but *p (the value of x) can
Neither p nor *p can be changed
p is a pointer to a constant integer

questions.question_en: In C, the statements char *s = "hello"; s[0] = 'H'; result in

s holding Hello on every compiler and system
a compilation error on every C compiler
s pointing to a fresh, writable copy of the string

Java always initialises array elements to default values. Numeric types get 0 (0.0 for double), boolean gets false, and reference types such as String get null. So the line prints 0 null false 0.0.

An interface can declare a public constructor
An interface can have default and static methods with a body
A class can implement only one interface at a time

A final class cannot be extended by another class
A final variable can be assigned a value only once
A blank final variable can be assigned in the constructor

questions.question_en: Which statement correctly describes how the JDK, JRE and JVM are related?

The JVM contains the JRE, and the JRE contains the JDK
The JRE contains the JDK, and the JDK contains the JVM
The JDK and the JRE do not use the JVM at all

questions.question_en: The Java compiler (javac) translates a .java source file into:

questions.question_en: Which statement about Java packages is TRUE?

An import statement copies the class code into the file
The java.lang package must always be imported explicitly

questions.question_en: In C++, what does the statement cin.ignore(100, '\n'); do?

Waits 100 milliseconds for the user to press the Enter key

questions.question_en: In a C++ program, the statement cin >> age; is followed by getline(cin, name);, and name gets an empty string. Why?

getline reads the newline that cin >> left in the input buffer

getline reads only from files and never from the keyboard

Is declared with the keyword abstract

When return x executes, the value 20 is saved as the return value. finally then runs and sets the local variable x to 30, but that does not change the value already saved. The method returns 20.

The exception is caught and the catch block prepares to return 2. The finally block always runs afterwards, and its own return 3 replaces the pending return value. So h() returns 3. (A return in finally is legal but bad practice, as it can hide exceptions.)

a has indexes 0 and 1, so a[2] = 5 throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException and A is skipped. Only the first matching catch runs, printing B. finally then prints D, and since the exception was handled, the program continues and prints E.

ArithmeticException is a subclass of Exception, so any ArithmeticException is already caught by the first block. The compiler reports the second catch as unreachable ("exception has already been caught"). More specific exceptions must be caught before more general ones.

questions.question_en: Which of the following is a checked exception in Java?
questions.explanation_en: Checked exceptions are subclasses of Exception that are not subclasses of RuntimeException; the compiler forces you to catch or declare them. IOException is checked. NullPointerException, ArithmeticException and ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException extend RuntimeException, so they are unchecked.

questions.question_en: In Java, which class is the direct superclass of both Exception and Error?
questions.explanation_en: java.lang.Throwable is the root of everything that can be thrown or caught; it has two direct subclasses, Exception and Error. RuntimeException and IOException are subclasses of Exception, and Thread is unrelated.

questions.question_en: In Java, the throws keyword is used to

options.en: declare in a method header the exceptions it may pass to its caller
throw an exception object explicitly from inside a block
catch every exception raised inside the method body
run clean-up code whether or not an exception occurs

questions.explanation_en: throws appears in a method declaration, for example void read() throws IOException, and tells callers which checked exceptions they must handle. throw (without s) is the statement that actually throws an exception object. Catching is done by catch, and clean-up by finally.

"1 " is printed, then throw 5 throws an int and the rest of the try block is skipped. Catch handlers are matched by type without the usual int-to-double conversion, so catch (double) is skipped and catch (int) receives 5. Output: 1 I5.

questions.question_en: In C++, if a thrown exception is not caught by any handler, which function is called automatically?
questions.explanation_en: When no matching catch is found, the C++ runtime calls std::terminate(), which by default calls std::abort() and ends the program abnormally. exit() and atexit() are for normal termination, and rethrow_exception() rethrows a stored exception.

questions.question_en:
What is the output of the following Python 3 code?
```python
def test(x):
    try:
        r = 10 // x
    except ZeroDivisionError:
        print("Z", end=" ")
    else:
        print("E", end=" ")
    finally:
        print("F", end=" ")

test(2)
test(0)
```
questions.explanation_en: test(2): no exception occurs, so the else block prints E, then finally prints F. test(0): 10 // 0 raises ZeroDivisionError, so except prints Z and else is skipped; finally still prints F. Output: E F Z F.

For "a", int("5") is 5 and 10 // 5 = 2. For "b", int("x") raises ValueError (right type, invalid value), so V is added. For "c", d["c"] raises KeyError because the key does not exist, so K is added. Result: 2VK.

questions.question_en: In Python 3, which exception is raised by the statement import xyzlib when no module named xyzlib is installed?
questions.explanation_en: When Python cannot find a module to import, it raises ModuleNotFoundError, which is a subclass of ImportError (so except ImportError also catches it). NameError is for an undefined name, FileNotFoundError for a missing file in open(), and AttributeError for a missing attribute.

questions.question_en: In Java, an ordinary try block (not try-with-resources) must be followed by

options.en: at least one catch block, a finally block, or both
exactly one catch block and exactly one finally block
a throws clause on the enclosing method

questions.explanation_en: A plain try must have at least one catch or a finally (or both); a try alone is a compilation error. It may have many catch blocks but at most one finally. A throws clause is optional and unrelated to this rule.

questions.question_en: In Java, in which of the following situations does the finally block NOT execute?

options.en: The try block executes a return statement
An exception is caught by a catch block
No exception is thrown in the try block
System.exit(0) is called inside the try block

questions.explanation_en: finally runs after normal completion, after a caught or uncaught exception, and even after return, break or continue. The main exception is System.exit(), which stops the JVM at once, so the finally block never runs (a JVM crash or power failure has the same effect).

questions.explanation_en: An identifier may contain letters, digits and underscores, cannot start with a digit, and cannot be a keyword. _total2 follows these rules. 2total starts with a digit, total-marks contains a hyphen (the minus operator), and for is a keyword.

questions.chapter: Programming — Python: Data Types, Collections, File Handling & Pandas
questions.question_en:
What is the output of the following Python code?
```python
print(chr(ord('a') - 32), ord('B') + 1)
```
questions.explanation_en: ord('a') is 97, and 97 - 32 = 65; chr(65) is 'A'. ord('B') is 66, and 66 + 1 = 67, which stays an int because chr() is not applied. print separates the two values with a space: A 67.

questions.chapter: Programming — Python: Data Types, Collections, File Handling & Pandas

What is the output of the following Python code?
```python
print(int("12") + float("3.5"), str(7) * 2)
```
questions.explanation_en: int("12") is 12 and float("3.5") is 3.5; int + float gives the float 15.5. str(7) is the string "7", and multiplying a string by 2 repeats it: "77". Output: 15.5 77.

questions.chapter: Programming — Python: Data Types, Collections, File Handling & Pandas
questions.question_en:
What is the output of the following Python code?
```python
print(17 // 5, 17 % 5, -17 // 5, 2 ** 3 ** 2)
```
questions.explanation_en: 17 // 5 = 3 and 17 % 5 = 2. Floor division rounds toward minus infinity, so -17 // 5 = floor(-3.4) = -4. ** is right-associative: 2 ** 3 ** 2 = 2 ** (3 ** 2) = 2 ** 9 = 512.

questions.chapter: Programming — Python: Data Types, Collections, File Handling & Pandas
questions.question_en:
What is the output of the following Python code?
```python
a = [1, 2]
b = [1, 2]
c = a
print(a == b, a is b, a is c)
```
questions.explanation_en: == compares values: a and b hold equal lists, so True. is compares identity: a and b are two separate list objects, so a is b is False. c = a binds c to the same object, so a is c is True.

questions.chapter: Programming — Python: Data Types, Collections, File Handling & Pandas
questions.question_en:

s = "DSSSB2024"
print(s[2:6], s[-4:], s[::-3])

questions.chapter: Programming — Python: Data Types, Collections, File Handling & Pandas
questions.question_en:
What is the output of the following Python code?
```python
print(max("Delhi"), min("Delhi"))
```
questions.explanation_en: max() and min() on a string compare Unicode (ASCII) values. D=68, e=101, l=108, h=104, i=105. The largest is 'l' (108). The smallest is the capital 'D' (68), because uppercase letters have smaller codes than lowercase ones.

questions.chapter: Programming — Python: Data Types, Collections, File Handling & Pandas

What is the output of the following Python code?

s = "  Delhi  "
print("[" + s.strip() + "]", len(s.rstrip()))
```
questions.explanation_en: strip() removes leading and trailing whitespace, giving "Delhi", so the first part prints [Delhi]. rstrip() removes only the trailing spaces, giving "  Delhi": 2 spaces + 5 letters = 7 characters.

questions.chapter: Programming — Python: Data Types, Collections, File Handling & Pandas

What is the output of the following Python code?

print("a,b,,c".split(","), len("a b  c".split()))
```
questions.explanation_en: With an explicit separator, split(",") cuts at every comma, so the two commas side by side give an empty string: ['a', 'b', '', 'c']. With no argument, split() splits on runs of whitespace and drops empty pieces, so "a b  c" gives ['a', 'b', 'c'], of length 3.

questions.chapter: Programming — Python: Data Types, Collections, File Handling & Pandas
questions.question_en: For a Python string s, what happens when the substring is NOT found by s.find(sub) and by s.index(sub)?

options.en: Both return -1 when sub is not found
Both return None when sub is not found

questions.explanation_en: Both methods return the lowest index where sub starts. They differ only when sub is absent: find() returns -1, while index() raises ValueError: substring not found.

questions.chapter: Programming — Python: Data Types, Collections, File Handling & Pandas
questions.question_en:
What is the output of the following Python code?
```python
L = [1, 2]
L.append([3, 4])
L.extend([5, 6])
print(len(L), L)
```
questions.explanation_en: append() adds its argument as one element, so the whole list [3, 4] becomes one item: [1, 2, [3, 4]]. extend() adds each element of the iterable separately: [1, 2, [3, 4], 5, 6]. That is 5 elements.

questions.chapter: Programming — Python: Data Types, Collections, File Handling & Pandas
questions.question_en:
What is the output of the following Python code?
```python
L = [3, 1, 2]
x = L.sort()
print(x, L)
```
questions.explanation_en: list.sort() sorts the list in place and returns None, like append(), extend(), insert(), remove() and reverse(). So x is None, and L itself is now [1, 2, 3]. Use sorted(L) when a new sorted list is wanted.

questions.chapter: Programming — Python: Data Types, Collections, File Handling & Pandas
questions.question_en:
What is the output of the following Python code?
```python
a = [1, 2, 3]
b = a
c = a[:]
b.append(4)
c.append(5)
print(a, len(c))
```
questions.explanation_en: b = a makes b another name (alias) for the same list, so b.append(4) changes a to [1, 2, 3, 4]. a[:] makes a new copy, so c is a separate list [1, 2, 3], and appending 5 to it does not affect a. len(c) is 4.

questions.chapter: Programming — Python: Data Types, Collections, File Handling & Pandas
questions.question_en:
What is the output of the following Python code?

L = [10, 20, 30, 40]
L.insert(1, 15)
L.pop()
L.remove(20)
print(L)
```
questions.explanation_en: insert(1, 15) puts 15 at index 1: [10, 15, 20, 30, 40]. pop() with no argument removes the last item (40): [10, 15, 20, 30]. remove(20) deletes the first element equal to 20: [10, 15, 30].

questions.chapter: Programming — Python: Data Types, Collections, File Handling & Pandas

What is the output of the following Python code?

print(L[8:2:-2], L[-3:])
```
questions.explanation_en: L is [0, 1, ..., 9]. L[8:2:-2] starts at index 8 and moves back by 2 while the index is greater than 2 (the stop is excluded): 8, 6, 4. L[-3:] gives the last three elements in their normal order: [7, 8, 9].

questions.chapter: Programming — Python: Data Types, Collections, File Handling & Pandas

What is the output of the following Python code?

t = (5)
u = (5,)
print(type(t).__name__, type(u).__name__, len(u))

questions.chapter: Programming — Python: Data Types, Collections, File Handling & Pandas

t = ("x", 10, "y", 20, "z")
print(t[1::2], t[-1], t.index("y"))
```
questions.explanation_en: t[1::2] starts at index 1 and takes every second element: indexes 1 and 3 give (10, 20). Slicing a tuple returns a tuple. t[-1] is the last element, z. t.index("y") gives the position of "y", which is 2.

questions.chapter: Programming — Python: Data Types, Collections, File Handling & Pandas
questions.question_en:
What is the output of the following Python code?
```python
t = (1, [2, 3])
t[1].append(4)
print(t, len(t))
```
questions.explanation_en: A tuple's own slots cannot be reassigned, but an object stored in a slot can change if it is mutable. t[1] is a list, and append() changes that list in place without assigning anything to the tuple, so there is no error. t becomes (1, [2, 3, 4]) and still has 2 elements.

questions.chapter: Programming — Python: Data Types, Collections, File Handling & Pandas
questions.question_en: Which pair of methods is available on a Python tuple object?
questions.explanation_en: A tuple is immutable, so it has only the two methods that do not change it: count(x) and index(x). append, extend, sort and reverse are list methods, and add/remove are set methods (list also has remove).

questions.chapter: Programming — Python: Data Types, Collections, File Handling & Pandas
questions.question_en:
What is the output of the following Python code?
```python
s = {3, 1, 3, 2, 1}
s.add(2)
s.add(4)
print(len(s), sorted(s))
```
questions.explanation_en: A set keeps only unique elements, so {3, 1, 3, 2, 1} is {1, 2, 3}. add(2) changes nothing because 2 is already there; add(4) adds 4. The set has 4 elements, and sorted() returns them as a sorted list: [1, 2, 3, 4].

questions.chapter: Programming — Python: Data Types, Collections, File Handling & Pandas
questions.explanation_en: & is intersection (common elements): {3, 4}. a - b keeps elements of a that are not in b: {1, 2}. a | b is the union {1, 2, 3, 4, 5}, of length 5. ^ is symmetric difference (in exactly one set): {1, 2, 5}.

questions.chapter: Programming — Python: Data Types, Collections, File Handling & Pandas
questions.question_en: Which of the following CANNOT be used as a key in a Python dictionary?
questions.explanation_en: Dictionary keys must be hashable, which in practice means immutable. Strings, numbers and tuples of immutable items can be keys. A list is mutable and unhashable, so {[1, 2]: 'x'} raises TypeError. Values can be of any type.

questions.chapter: Programming — Python: Data Types, Collections, File Handling & Pandas

What is the output of the following Python code?
```python
d = {'a': 1, 'b': 2, 'a': 3}
print(d, len(d))
```
questions.explanation_en: Keys are unique. When a key is repeated, the later value replaces the earlier one, but the key keeps its first position. So 'a' stays first with value 3, and the dictionary has 2 items.

questions.chapter: Programming — Python: Data Types, Collections, File Handling & Pandas

What is the output of the following Python code?

d = {'x': 10}
print(d.get('y'), d.get('y', 0), d.setdefault('z', 5), len(d))
```
questions.explanation_en: get('y') returns None for a missing key instead of raising KeyError. get('y', 0) returns the default 0, and neither call adds a key. setdefault('z', 5) inserts 'z': 5 because 'z' is missing and returns 5. d now has 2 keys.

questions.question_en: In Python 3.7 and later, what does d.popitem() remove from a dictionary d?

options.en: The pair with the smallest key

questions.explanation_en: From Python 3.7, dictionaries keep insertion order, and popitem() removes and returns the most recently inserted (key, value) pair (LIFO order). It raises KeyError if the dictionary is empty. pop(key) removes a chosen key.

questions.chapter: Programming — Python: Data Types, Collections, File Handling & Pandas

add(1)
print(add(2), add(3, []))

questions.explanation_en: *nums collects all positional arguments into a tuple. stats(4, 5, 6) returns len 3 and sum 15. Writing return a, b returns a tuple, which prints as (3, 15). stats() returns (0, 0), whose type is tuple.

options.en: The pandas module was found but contains a syntax error
pandas was imported successfully but is an old version
The program file was not saved with a .py extension

questions.explanation_en: import math as m binds the module only to the name m, so its functions are used as m.sqrt(25), which gives 5.0. The name math is not defined, and sqrt alone would need from math import sqrt.

questions.chapter: Programming — Python: Data Types, Collections, File Handling & Pandas
questions.question_en: Which file mode opens a file for both reading and appending, creates the file if it does not exist, and sends every write to the end of the file?
questions.explanation_en: a+ opens for appending and reading, creates a missing file, and always writes at the end, keeping the old data. r+ is read/write with the pointer at the start and needs an existing file. w+ is write/read but empties the file first. rb is read-only binary.

questions.chapter: Programming — Python: Data Types, Collections, File Handling & Pandas
questions.question_en: Which file mode opens a file for writing and reading but first erases any existing contents?
questions.explanation_en: w and w+ truncate an existing file to zero length, or create it if it is missing. w+ also allows reading. r+ keeps the contents and starts at the beginning, a+ keeps the contents and writes at the end, and rb only reads in binary.

questions.chapter: Programming — Python: Data Types, Collections, File Handling & Pandas
questions.question_en: Which of the following modes raises FileNotFoundError when the file does not already exist?
questions.explanation_en: The read modes (r, r+, rb, rb+) need an existing file and raise FileNotFoundError otherwise. The modes w, w+, a and a+ create the file if it is missing.

with open("notes.txt") as f:
    a = f.readline()
    b = f.read(3)

print(repr(a), b, len(c))

readline() reads one line including its newline, so a is 'one
'. read(3) reads the next 3 characters: two. The pointer is now just before the newline after two, so readlines() returns ['
', 'three
'], a list of length 2.

questions.chapter: Programming — Python: Data Types, Collections, File Handling & Pandas
questions.question_en:
What is the output of the following Python code?
```python
with open("s.txt", "w") as f:
    n = f.write("PYTHON")
with open("s.txt") as f:
    f.seek(2)
    x = f.read(3)
    print(n, x, f.tell())
```
questions.explanation_en: write() returns the number of characters written: 6. seek(2) moves the file pointer to offset 2, which is the character T (P=0, Y=1, T=2). read(3) reads THO, and the pointer moves on to offset 5, which tell() reports.

questions.chapter: Programming — Python: Data Types, Collections, File Handling & Pandas
questions.question_en: What is the main advantage of opening a file with with open('a.txt') as f: ?

options.en: The file is opened in both read and write mode together
The whole file is loaded into memory before any reading
The file is closed automatically, even if an error occurs
The file is locked so no other program can open it

questions.explanation_en: with uses the file object as a context manager. When the block ends, normally or because of an exception, the file's close() is called automatically. This avoids leaving files open and losing data that has not been written yet.

questions.chapter: Programming — Python: Data Types, Collections, File Handling & Pandas
questions.question_en:
What is the output of the following Python code?
```python
with open("log.txt", "w") as f:
    f.write("12")
with open("log.txt", "w") as f:
    f.write("34")
with open("log.txt", "a") as f:
    f.write("56")
with open("log.txt") as f:
    print(f.read())
```
questions.explanation_en: The first 'w' writes 12. The second 'w' truncates the file, so 12 is lost and the file holds 34. 'a' keeps the contents and adds 56 at the end, giving 3456. The final read prints 3456.

questions.chapter: Programming — Python: Data Types, Collections, File Handling & Pandas
questions.question_en:
What is the output of the following Python code?
```python
import csv
with open("marks.csv", "w", newline="") as f:
    w = csv.writer(f)
    w.writerow(["roll", "marks"])
    w.writerow([1, 95])
with open("marks.csv", newline="") as f:
    rows = list(csv.reader(f))
print(rows[1], len(rows))
```
questions.explanation_en: The file has two lines: roll,marks and 1,95. csv.reader returns each line as a list of strings; it does not convert numbers. So rows[1] is ['1', '95'], and rows has 2 rows, the header included.

questions.chapter: Programming — Python: Data Types, Collections, File Handling & Pandas
questions.question_en: Which csv.writer method writes every row of a list of lists in a single call?
questions.explanation_en: writerow(row) writes one row, and writerows(rows) writes every row of an iterable of rows. writelines() is a method of ordinary file objects that writes strings without CSV formatting. There is no writeall() method.

questions.chapter: Programming — Python: Data Types, Collections, File Handling & Pandas
questions.question_en:
What is the output of the following Python code?
```python
import pandas as pd
s = pd.Series([10, 20, 30], index=['a', 'b', 'c'])
print(s['b'] + s.iloc[2], len(s))
```
questions.explanation_en: A Series is a one-dimensional labelled array. s['b'] picks by label and gives 20; s.iloc[2] picks by position (0-based) and gives 30. 20 + 30 = 50, and the Series has 3 elements.

questions.chapter: Programming — Python: Data Types, Collections, File Handling & Pandas
questions.question_en:
What is the output of the following Python code?
```python
import pandas as pd
df = pd.DataFrame({'name': ['A', 'B', 'C'], 'marks': [70, 85, 90]})
print(df.shape, df['marks'].max())
```
questions.explanation_en: Each dictionary key becomes a column and each list holds that column's values. There are 3 rows and 2 columns, so shape is (rows, columns) = (3, 2). df['marks'].max() is 90.

questions.chapter: Programming — Python: Data Types, Collections, File Handling & Pandas
questions.question_en:
What is the output of the following Python code?
```python
import pandas as pd
s = pd.Series([5, 6, 7, 8], index=[1, 2, 3, 4])
print(s.loc[1:3].sum(), s.iloc[1:3].sum())
```
questions.explanation_en: loc slices by label and includes the end label, so s.loc[1:3] takes labels 1, 2 and 3: 5 + 6 + 7 = 18. iloc slices by position and excludes the end, like a Python list, so s.iloc[1:3] takes positions 1 and 2: 6 + 7 = 13.

questions.chapter: Programming — Python: Data Types, Collections, File Handling & Pandas
questions.question_en:
What is the output of the following Python code?
```python
import pandas as pd
df1 = pd.DataFrame({'A': [1, 2], 'B': [3, 4]})
df2 = pd.DataFrame({'A': [5, 6], 'B': [7, 8]})
print(pd.concat([df1, df2]).shape, pd.concat([df1, df2], axis=1).shape)
```
questions.explanation_en: pd.concat() joins along axis 0 by default, stacking the rows: 2 + 2 = 4 rows and the same 2 columns, so (4, 2). With axis=1 the frames are placed side by side: 2 rows and 2 + 2 = 4 columns, so (2, 4).

questions.chapter: Programming — Python: Data Types, Collections, File Handling & Pandas

What is the output of the following Python code?

import pandas as pd
left = pd.DataFrame({'id': [1, 2, 3], 'name': ['Asha', 'Ravi', 'Gita']})
right = pd.DataFrame({'id': [2, 3, 4], 'marks': [50, 60, 70]})

import pandas as pd

questions.question_en: In .NET, which component manages memory (garbage collection), security and exception handling while a program runs?
questions.explanation_en: The CLR is the .NET execution engine and sits between the application and the operating system. It loads code, JIT-compiles it, and provides garbage collection, type safety, security and exception handling.

questions.question_en: In .NET, the Just-In-Time (JIT) compiler converts:

options.en: C# source code into MSIL code at compile time
MSIL (CIL) code into native machine code at run time
Native machine code back into MSIL code
VB.NET source code into equivalent C# code

questions.explanation_en: .NET language compilers first produce MSIL (CIL), a CPU-independent intermediate code. When a method is first called, the CLR's JIT compiler turns that MSIL into native code for the current CPU.

questions.question_en: The set of basic rules that a .NET language must follow so that its code can be used from other .NET languages is the:
questions.explanation_en: The CLS is a subset of the CTS. It lists the rules that every CLS-compliant language and library must follow (for example, public members should not use unsigned types such as uint). This makes language interoperability possible: a VB.NET program can use a C# library.

questions.question_en: In .NET, C# int and VB.NET Integer both map to System.Int32. Which component defines this common set of types?
questions.explanation_en: The CTS defines how types are declared, used and managed in the runtime, so all .NET languages share one type system. Language keywords such as int (C#) and Integer (VB.NET) are aliases for the same CTS type, System.Int32.

questions.question_en: Code that runs under the control of the CLR, which handles its memory and security, is called:
questions.explanation_en: Managed code is executed by the CLR, which provides garbage collection, type checking and security. Unmanaged code, such as a C++ program compiled straight to machine code, runs directly on the operating system without CLR services.

questions.question_en: In .NET, the Global Assembly Cache (GAC) is used to store:

options.en: Temporary files created by the JIT compiler at run time
Source code files of all installed .NET applications
Objects that the garbage collector has not yet freed
Strong-named assemblies shared by several applications

questions.explanation_en: An assembly (.dll or .exe) is the unit of deployment in .NET and holds MSIL plus a manifest. A private assembly sits in its application's folder. A shared assembly must have a strong name and is installed in the GAC so that many applications can use it.

questions.question_en: Which programming language, designed by Anders Hejlsberg, was released by Microsoft with .NET Framework 1.0 in 2002?
questions.explanation_en: Microsoft released .NET Framework 1.0 in 2002, together with C# 1.0, a language designed by Anders Hejlsberg's team. Java is from Sun Microsystems (now Oracle), Kotlin is from JetBrains and Swift is from Apple.

questions.question_en: Which statement about a static constructor in C# is TRUE?

options.en: It can be overloaded with different parameter lists
It must be called explicitly using the new keyword
It has no parameters and runs once, before the class is first used
It runs again each time a new object is created

questions.explanation_en: A static constructor takes no parameters and no access modifier, and a class can have only one. The CLR calls it automatically, exactly once, before the first instance is created or any static member is used. It is used to initialise static data.

questions.question_en: Which statement about a constructor in C# is TRUE?

options.en: It must always be declared with the return type void
It can be called only once in the whole program
A class is allowed to have only one constructor
It has the same name as its class and no return type

questions.explanation_en: A C# constructor has the same name as the class and no return type, not even void. It runs automatically when an object is created with new. Constructors can be overloaded, and the compiler supplies a default one if none is written.

questions.question_en: Which of the following is a value type in C#?
questions.explanation_en: Value types (int, double, bool, char, enum and struct) hold their data directly, usually on the stack. class, interface, string, arrays and delegates are reference types: the variable holds a reference to an object on the managed heap.

questions.question_en: In C#, the statement object o = 25; converts a value type into a reference type. This conversion is called:
questions.explanation_en: Boxing wraps a value type in an object on the heap, so it can be treated as System.Object. The reverse, int n = (int)o;, is unboxing and needs an explicit cast.

questions.question_en: In C#, a class member declared internal can be accessed:

options.en: Only in classes derived from it

questions.explanation_en: internal limits access to the current assembly (the same .dll or .exe). private allows only the containing class, protected allows the class and its derived classes, and public allows any code. protected internal combines protected and internal.

questions.question_en: Which C# collection stores key-value pairs with unique keys and compile-time type safety, as a generic replacement for Hashtable?
questions.explanation_en: Hashtable (System.Collections) stores key-value pairs and finds a value by its unique key, but keys and values are just object. Dictionary<TKey, TValue> (System.Collections.Generic) does the same with type safety. List<T> and ArrayList are accessed by index, and Queue<T> is FIFO.

questions.question_en: In VB.NET, which control lets the user select several options from a group at the same time?
questions.explanation_en: Each CheckBox can be ticked or cleared on its own, so any number can be selected. RadioButtons in one group are mutually exclusive, so only one can be selected. A Label shows text and a TextBox takes typed input.

questions.question_en: Which VB.NET control combines a text box with a drop-down list, so the user can pick an item or type a value?
questions.explanation_en: A ComboBox is a text box with a drop-down list. A ListBox shows a list that is always visible and has no editable text area. A CheckBox is a single on/off option, and a PictureBox shows an image.

questions.chapter: Programming — Programming Basics: Data Types, Operators & Control Flow
questions.question_en: How many primitive data types are defined in Java?
questions.explanation_en: Java has exactly eight primitive types: byte, short, int, long, float, double, char and boolean. String, arrays and classes are reference types, not primitives.

questions.chapter: Programming — Programming Basics: Data Types, Operators & Control Flow
questions.explanation_en: A byte holds -128 to 127, and a narrowing cast keeps only the low 8 bits. 200 does not fit, so it wraps to 200 - 256 = -56. Likewise 130 becomes 130 - 256 = -126.

questions.chapter: Programming — Programming Basics: Data Types, Operators & Control Flow
questions.explanation_en: In C (C99 onwards) integer division truncates toward zero, so -23 / 4 = -5.75 becomes -5. The remainder follows a == (a/b)*b + a%b, so -23 % 4 = -23 - (-20) = -3. The remainder takes the sign of the dividend; -6 1 would be Python's floor-division result.

questions.chapter: Programming — Programming Basics: Data Types, Operators & Control Flow
questions.question_en:
What is the output of the following Python 3 code?
```python
print(7 / 2, -17 // 5, -17 % 5)
```
questions.explanation_en: In Python 3, / is true division, so 7 / 2 = 3.5. // is floor division: -17 / 5 = -3.4, floored down to -4. % takes the sign of the divisor, so -17 % 5 = -17 - (-4*5) = 3.

questions.chapter: Programming — Programming Basics: Data Types, Operators & Control Flow
questions.question_en: In Java, given `byte b = 10;`, which of the following statements causes a compilation error?
questions.explanation_en: In b + 5 the byte is promoted to int, so the result is an int, and an int cannot be assigned to a byte without an explicit cast. Compound assignment (+=) and ++ include an automatic cast back to byte, so they compile. The explicit (byte) cast also compiles.

questions.chapter: Programming — Programming Basics: Data Types, Operators & Control Flow
questions.explanation_en: + is evaluated left to right. 1 + 2 are both ints, so they add to 3. 3 + "3" is a String, "33", and from then on every + is concatenation: "334", then "3345".

questions.chapter: Programming — Programming Basics: Data Types, Operators & Control Flow
questions.explanation_en: j = i++ stores the old value 10 in j, then i becomes 11. k = ++i first makes i 12, then stores 12 in k. So i = 12, j = 10, k = 12.

questions.chapter: Programming — Programming Basics: Data Types, Operators & Control Flow
questions.explanation_en: In Java, i = i++ first saves the old value of i (0), then increments i to 1, and finally assigns the saved 0 back to i. So each pass leaves i at 0. After four passes it is still 0.

questions.chapter: Programming — Programming Basics: Data Types, Operators & Control Flow
questions.explanation_en: *, / and % have higher precedence than + and -, and they group left to right. b * c / 2 = 12 / 2 = 6 and a % b = 10 % 4 = 2. Then 10 - 6 + 2 = 6.

questions.chapter: Programming — Programming Basics: Data Types, Operators & Control Flow
questions.explanation_en: Relational operators give 1 (true) or 0 (false) and group left to right. 10 > x > 2 is (10 > 5) > 2, which is 1 > 2, so 0. In the second expression > has higher precedence than ==, so it is (10 > 5) == 1, which is 1 == 1, so 1.

questions.chapter: Programming — Programming Basics: Data Types, Operators & Control Flow
questions.explanation_en: || and && evaluate left to right with a sequence point after the left operand. b++ gives 0 (false) and b becomes 1, so a-- is evaluated: it gives 2 (true) and a becomes 1. The left side of && is therefore 1, so ++b runs: b becomes 2, which is true. A logical result is always 0 or 1, so c = 1, giving 1 2 1.

questions.chapter: Programming — Programming Basics: Data Types, Operators & Control Flow
questions.explanation_en: && short-circuits: a > 5 is false, so ++a is skipped and a stays 3; r is false. & on booleans always evaluates both sides, so ++a runs and a becomes 4, but false & true is still false. Output: 4 false false.

questions.chapter: Programming — Programming Basics: Data Types, Operators & Control Flow
questions.explanation_en: In binary a = 1100 and b = 1010. AND gives 1000 = 8, OR gives 1110 = 14, and XOR (1 where the bits differ) gives 0110 = 6.

questions.chapter: Programming — Programming Basics: Data Types, Operators & Control Flow
questions.explanation_en: In two's complement ~x equals -(x + 1), so ~5 = -6. x << 3 multiplies by 2^3: 5 * 8 = 40. x >> 1 divides a positive value by 2 and drops the fraction: 5 >> 1 = 2.

questions.chapter: Programming — Programming Basics: Data Types, Operators & Control Flow
questions.explanation_en: >> is the signed right shift: it copies the sign bit, so -16 >> 2 = -16 / 4 = -4. >>> is the unsigned right shift: it fills with zeros. -16 is 0xFFFFFFF0, and shifting it right by 28 leaves the top four 1-bits, 1111 = 15.

questions.chapter: Programming — Programming Basics: Data Types, Operators & Control Flow
questions.question_en:
What is the output of the following Python 3 code?

print(2 ** 3 ** 2, -2 ** 2)
```
questions.explanation_en: ** is right-associative, so 2 ** 3 ** 2 = 2 ** (3 ** 2) = 2 ** 9 = 512. ** also binds more tightly than unary minus, so -2 ** 2 = -(2 ** 2) = -4.

questions.chapter: Programming — Programming Basics: Data Types, Operators & Control Flow
questions.explanation_en: a / b divides two ints, so the result is the int 3, which is then stored in f as 3.0. In (float)a / b the cast applies to a first, so 7.0 / 2 is a floating-point division giving 3.5. %.1f prints one decimal place: 3.0 3.5.

questions.chapter: Programming — Programming Basics: Data Types, Operators & Control Flow
questions.question_en: In C, which format specifier must be used with scanf() to read a value into a variable of type double?
questions.explanation_en: scanf() needs a pointer of the exact type. %f expects a float *, %lf expects a double * and %Lf expects a long double *. (In printf(), %f works for double too, because float arguments are promoted to double.)

questions.chapter: Programming — Programming Basics: Data Types, Operators & Control Flow
questions.question_en: In C, the library functions sqrt() and pow() are declared in which header file?
questions.explanation_en: Mathematical functions such as sqrt(), pow(), sin() and floor() are declared in <math.h>. stdio.h holds input/output functions like printf() and scanf(), and stdlib.h holds functions like malloc() and atoi().

questions.chapter: Programming — Programming Basics: Data Types, Operators & Control Flow
questions.question_en: In C, which operation is NOT allowed on a variable declared with the register storage class?

options.en: Taking its address with the & operator
Assigning a new value to it
Using it as a loop counter
Passing its value to a function

questions.explanation_en: register asks the compiler to keep the variable in a CPU register for fast access. Because a register has no memory address, the C standard forbids applying & to a register variable, even if the compiler actually keeps it in memory. Reading, assigning and passing its value are all allowed.
